items.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: I spent a lot of time as a kid listening to saxophone players as much as I listened to clarinet players because I mean it’s amazing the things you can learn listening to Lester Young or John Coltrane or Charlie Parker or Coleman Hawkins or any one of these guys.

ctx.x: The state of jazz on the radio, and stuff that’s coming out currently, does it affect your own playing much? Do you listen to the contemporary young guys playing?

Yes, constantly. And I will say that there seems to be more jazz on the radio now than there was say ten years ago. But most of the stations are public radio stations or college stations and so forth. In Orlando we have WUCF which is an excellent jazz station. Now it depends on what you’re talking about. If you’re talking about the stuff that they call smooth jazz, no, I don’t listen to that stuff at all. I don’t consider that jazz, I consider that a kind of a smooth form of rock & roll. Because I don’t know who…
What’s it like trying to find outlets for recording these days? You get hooked up with a good label and try to stay with them?
